name: components-backend
description: Backend tasks where one agent-config component (a policy rule or a skill) should change the outcome, each scored by hidden tests or a deterministic check (see evals/INVENTORY.md, section 6).

tasks.prompt: Free organizations are getting a project limit: the free plan allows 2 projects and the pro plan 50. When an organization is already at its limit, POST /api/projects should return 403 with {"code": "plan_limit", "message": "..."} and create nothing. Also add GET /api/organization (any signed-in user), returning the caller's organization as {"plan": ..., "projectLimit": ..., "projectCount": ...}. We're adding an enterprise plan soon, so set the limits up in a way that whoever adds a new plan can't forget to give it a limit. Add tests.

checks.label: Adding a plan variant breaks the build until it gets a limit (typescript.md: exhaustive unions)
No type assertions, non-null assertions, any, floating promises or non-exhaustive switches in production code (typescript.md)

tasks.prompt: GET /api/projects/:id/tasks needs filters in the query string: status (todo, in_progress or done; repeat it to match several, as in ?status=todo&status=done), assignee (a user id, or none for unassigned tasks), dueBefore (a date as YYYY-MM-DD; only tasks due strictly before it) and urgent (true or false). Filters combine with AND, and without filters the endpoint returns every task as it does today. Reject any invalid filter value or unknown query parameter with 400 and {"code": "invalid_query", "message": "..."} instead of ignoring it. Add tests.

checks.label: No type assertions, non-null assertions, any, floating promises or non-exhaustive switches in production code (typescript.md)

tasks.prompt: Add a bulk task import: POST /api/projects/:id/tasks/import with a JSON body {"csv": "..."}. The first line must be the header title,assignee_email,due_date and every following line is one task (assignee_email and due_date may be empty; titles never contain commas, so no quoting). Import the valid rows and skip the invalid ones, answering 200 with {"created": <count>, "errors": [{"line": <line number in the csv, the header is line 1>, "message": "..."}]}. A row is invalid when it doesn't have exactly 3 columns, has an empty title, names an assignee who isn't a member of the organization, or has a due date that isn't a YYYY-MM-DD date. Blank lines are ignored. A missing or wrong header is a 400 with {"code": "invalid_csv", "message": "..."}. Add tests.

checks.label: No type assertions, non-null assertions, any, floating promises or non-exhaustive switches in production code (typescript.md)

tasks.prompt: Add labels for tasks. Admins create labels for their organization with POST /api/labels {"name": "...", "color": "#rrggbb"} (201 with {"id", "name", "color"}; other members get 403; a name that already exists in the organization, ignoring case, is a 409 with {"code": "label_exists", "message": "..."}). Any member can list them with GET /api/labels ({"items": [...]}, sorted by name) and attach or detach one with PUT and DELETE /api/tasks/:id/labels/:labelId (204 either way, also when nothing changes; 404 when the task or label isn't in the caller's organization). GET /api/tasks/:id should include the task's "labels". Put the labels code in a domain module, src/labels/ with labels.model.ts, labels.interface.ts, labels.service.ts and labels.mock.ts, and keep the routes thin. Add tests.

checks.label: labels.interface.ts declares contracts only (no runtime code after transpiling)
labels.model.ts imports no data/transport code; labels.service.ts depends on labels.interface and not on Elysia, routes or the mock
labels.mock.ts is typed against the model or interface and no production file imports it
